answer:
**Only `a.log` is excluded by `--exclude-ext=log` itself.**

The value is stored verbatim as `"log"` (src/main.zig:1480-1483) and matched by `matchesExt` (src/filter.zig:297-306), which requires a `.` right before the suffix (src/filter.zig:302) and compares bytes exactly, case-sensitively (src/filter.zig:300,303).

- `a.log` — **yes**: the `.` precedes `log` (src/filter.zig:302-303).
- `catalog` — **no**: it ends with `log`, but the preceding char is `a`, not `.` (src/filter.zig:302).
- `.log` — **no**: the name is exactly the extension, so no stem-plus-dot exists (src/filter.zig:302). It *is* still excluded by default because `".log"` is in the built-in list (src/filter.zig:40, src/filter.zig:598-602), unless `--no-default-ignore`/`--no-ignore` (src/main.zig:2424); `--no-hidden` also skips it as a dotfile (src/filter.zig:594, src/main.zig:1457-1458).
- `A.LOG` — **no**: matching is case-sensitive (src/filter.zig:300,303).

Caveat: a file named explicitly on the command line bypasses the filter (src/main.zig:2582-2587). Verified with the built binary: `--no-default-ignore --exclude-ext=log` matched only `catalog` and `A.LOG`.
